chunks: 4168 - And ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from al-Fuḍayl, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who slaughtered, and the knife got ahead of him and severed the head. So he said: “It is a valid slaughter while the animal is alive, so there is no harm in eating it.”

key_terms.السِّكِّينُ: the knife used in the act of slaughtering
key_terms.ذَبَحَ: he slaughtered an animal according to the act under discussion
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection
key_terms.وَحِيَّةٌ: while the animal was still alive

ai.seo_question: Is an animal halal to eat if the head is accidentally severed completely during slaughter?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on an animal whose head is severed during slaughter because the knife moved too quickly. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام rules that the slaughter is valid and the animal is permissible to eat, so long as the slaughter occurred while it was alive.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4168 - Umar ibn Udhaynah narrated from Al-Fudayl who said:

I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man who was slaughtering an animal, and the knife moved too quickly and severed the head completely.
Imam (as) said: "It is a valid slaughtering, and there is no harm in eating it."
